name: roleboard-image-v1
description: Asset- and cast-level evaluation for AutoDrama roleboard generation and downstream prompt validation.

scale.8: strong production result with minor defects
scale.10: exceptional, specific, clean, and fully supported

dimensions.question: Is there exactly one front, one true profile, and one back full-body view in that order, with no extra panel or angle?
Are all heads and feet visible at equal scale on a shared baseline with clean spacing and useful margins?
Do age, gender presentation, identity invariants, wardrobe facts, status, and declared variant changes match the source contract?
Do face, skull, hair, body, garments, footwear, palette, and signature details remain the same identity across all views?
Did the template affect only layout and the key vision only style, without copied people, armor, sword, crown, pose, or scenery?
Is the face defined by readable, role-specific geometry and age evidence rather than a generic beauty archetype?
Are head-to-body ratio, build, torso, hips, limbs, posture, age, occupation, and health plausible and intentional?
Do silhouette, layers, closures, footwear, material, wear, palette, and ornament fit role, era, status, and all three views?
Is the design memorable but restrained, without random filigree, over-armoring, excessive jewelry, glowing trim, or game-skin clutter?
Do medium, facial rendering, material response, palette, light character, and finish belong to the key vision?
Are face, ears, neck, shoulders, hands, fingers, legs, feet, profile, and back anatomy clean and plausible?
Is the output free of labels, text, watermark, logo, frame lines, collage marks, stray props, and unexplained objects?
Can the board immediately serve as a stable identity reference for downstream image and video nodes?
Can every role pair be distinguished by face geometry without relying only on hair, clothes, age label, or color?
Do body build, posture, hair mass, garment outline, and proportion distinguish roles at thumbnail scale?
Do costumes encode different age, status, and function while remaining in the same culture?
Do rendering, materials, palette family, lighting, and design culture remain one project across the cast?
Does the cast avoid repeated oval faces, identical eyes and jaws, porcelain skin, generic hair, random filigree, and symmetric AI concept-art polish?

gates.description: Exactly the required front/profile/back views and no others.
All views show one consistent identity.
Required anatomy and clothing are complete and visible.
No source age, gender, identity, wardrobe, or variant contradiction.
No spatial-template or key-vision identity, prop, costume, or scene leakage.
No production-breaking facial, hand, limb, or body defect.
No extra subject, prop, text, watermark, logo, or collage artifact.
The cast does not reuse a near-identical face, body, or costume base.
Variants remain recognizably the same role with only authorized changes.
Every role remains in the same validated rendering medium and style family.
